brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Four-cell single-storey base (full cells at -1,0; 0,0; 1,0 plus half cell 0,1) dressed with electronics props: M3 screw, nut and standoff heaps (prop:1, prop:2, prop:3, prop:5) in the bin compartments.
piece: -1,0,0;full, 0,0,0;full, 1,0,0;full and 0,1,0;half-s, joined as one body (check_build: single group), joint bolts locked and open faces capped.
bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) are drop-in trays that lift out, filled with screw/nut/standoff heaps.
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the cut face of the half-s base at 0,1,0; the blocking prop was removed so its pull is clear.

handle:0,0,0;top mounted on cover:0,0,0;full;top (chained inserts 60/180/300) over the centre cell, clear of the bins either side. Note: the configurator checks fit only, so the handle's load rating for carrying the loaded organizer is not verified.

finish.summary: Portable electronics organizer on a 4-cell hexagonal base: two removable divided drop-in bins (2- and 3-compartment) flanking the centre cell, a drawer on the front half-cell, and a carry handle on the central top cover. Bins are filled with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. Open faces are capped, joints bolted, check_build passes with meshClash clear and no warnings. Carry-weight strength of the handle is outside what the configurator can verify.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
